### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**72** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `current_user (literal, 44 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 56 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `1e99b932a9de8770ca9c062b192b9397dac87ef7` — the merge of head `6e244858be3dcfd43422aff2f5dbd64a5a74f972` into base `f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 1e99b932a9de8770ca9c062b192b9397dac87ef7 && git checkout 1e99b932a9de8770ca9c062b192b9397dac87ef7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587 6e244858be3dcfd43422aff2f5dbd64a5a74f972 && git checkout -B drift-repro f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587 && git merge --no-ff 6e244858be3dcfd43422aff2f5dbd64a5a74f972

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f4dbcc2153566226f283c79c73255369c2c97587` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 full · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `6e244858be3dcfd43422aff2f5dbd64a5a74f972` · card #34780 (`Part of #34780`) · full read at `bdcf01ec`, then the delta `bdcf01ec..6e244858` · read 2026-11-19T01:29Z

Net diff against merge base `cdb327fdf03`: 6 files, +474 / -28, all of them in `@objectstack/scenarios` plus one changeset. The door mode rules arm gains a built-in corpus, `--door-rules builtin`, ported as one data module.

### The maintainer's word

- **The port is on the maintainer's own word, in two records.** The decision card chose "Yes, port it now" (2026-11-18 17:44Z), and his own reply was 「同意你执行」 (2026-11-19 00:12Z). I read both in the area's thread, not as relays. This supersedes the earlier constraint that no hosted text be copied.

### Against the card

- **`Part of` is right.** The card is done when a five-reps round is on record. This PR removes the need for a rules file kept outside the repository for that round. The round itself is still the maintainer's.

### Read at the head

- **The source is named.** The PR body and the module header both name `objectstack-ai/cloud` at `c9b6664d9ac8cdc16df61a40febe3b5c71f41f11`, the rendering call, and the eight source files under `packages/service-ai-studio/src/`. The published sections each rule ends with are read from this repository's own `skills/` at the base commit, and both texts say so.
- **The scrub, read entry by entry.** I extracted all 56 texts and scanned each one, and read every hit in context:
  - **Addresses.** The only URLs are the `example.com` samples already public in `skills/` and the placeholder `url:'https://…'`. There is no hostname, no `localhost` and no IP address.
  - **Secrets and keys.** There is no key-shaped string. Every hit on "secret", "token", "credential" or "password" is authoring guidance: never put a credential in a flow, `secret` vs `password` field types, and `credentialRef`. None of them is a value.
  - **Tenant and customer data.** The "live failure" anecdotes are generic, with no organization, person or environment named. One cites a masked sample phone number from a build's own sample rows.
  - **Control-plane-only text.** `14b-tier` (the hosted runtime's timer lifecycle) is the one rule left out, and the five rules the door's tier does not offer are absent. What remains describes authoring behaviour, the build door's tools and the platform's published rules.
  - **Tracker ids.** No `cloud#` id remains. The 13 struck citations are declared as the one deviation from verbatim.
  - **The new test.** It scans for these kinds of content and holds planted positives that prove it can fail.
- **Wiring.**
  - `--door-rules builtin` (or `OS_SCENARIOS_DOOR_RULES=builtin`) goes through the same judge as a rules file. The record states the arm as `builtin` with the sha256 of its JSON.
  - A rules file is still read as before. With no `--door-rules` the arm has no rules, so existing door records keep their meaning. A file literally named `builtin` is passed with a path.
- **Sets.** There are five named sets, each pinned. `names-build-door-tools` is derived from `PLATFORM_TOOLS_BY_PACKAGE['service-ai-studio']`, and `omit ondemand` leaves exactly `inline`.
- **Changeset, read sentence by sentence.** It is one file for `@objectstack/scenarios`, at `patch`, opening on its title line. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right: no product package and no authorable surface moves. Each statement matches the code.
- **Merges** cleanly onto origin/main `f4dbcc2153`.
- **Check-runs at this head:** 49 in total, all completed, none failed (33 `success`, 16 `skipped`).

### Delta `bdcf01ec..6e244858`

- **One test line changed in `door.test.ts`, the fix for the Test Core 5/10 red at `bdcf01ec`.** The CLI-wiring case no longer builds the live `claude` driver, whose version probe needs the CLI on PATH. It now asserts that `makeDriver('claude', { doorRules: 'builtin', doorRulesOmit: 'rule-z' })` throws `DoorRulesRefusedError`. That pins that `makeDriver` reads and judges the built-in corpus before it builds the driver. The accepting path is still pinned directly through `readDoorRules(BUILTIN_DOOR_RULES, { omit: 'ondemand' })` in the same case. No source file moved.

### Not mine, still owed

- Landing, through the seat. After merge, the five-reps round is the maintainer's (`RULES=builtin`).
